proposal.hypothesis: The three valid direct-path variants measured so far were slightly slower in complete-run aggregates than baseline, but those aggregates do not isolate small n. Test whether CUDA Cooperative Groups' integer block reduction can make the direct path cheaper than the hand-coded shared-memory or warp-shuffle variants: dispatch 2 <= n <= 512 to one 128-thread CTA, where each thread accumulates at most four values and the CTA writes directly to out. Preserve n=1 as a copy-only control and leave the staged path above 512 unchanged. This is a performance hypothesis, not an assumed speedup.

retained: Add a one-CTA small-input reduction using cg::reduce and cg::plus<int>; each of 128 threads sums strided elements and the block result is written directly to out.
Dispatch 2 <= n <= 512 to the direct reduction, using four elements per thread as a generic bound.
Keep n=1 on its existing device-copy behavior and preserve the existing staged reduction path for n > 512.

proposal.hypothesis: Prior direct-path complete-run means (46.9589–47.0667 μs) were slightly above the 46.7866 μs baseline, but they do not isolate small-n costs. Test a narrower generic crossover: for 2 <= n <= 32, use one full warp with one lane per input and a direct output write; keep n=1 copy-only and use the staged path above one warp. This tests whether the smallest nontrivial inputs benefit without assuming that a kernel launch beats the copy path.

retained: Replace the shared-memory cooperative-groups small reduction with a one-warp reduction using the existing warpReduceSum helper.
Dispatch only 2 <= n <= 32 to the direct kernel, using the generic 32-lane warp capacity; preserve n=1 copy-only behavior and leave the staged path for larger inputs unchanged.
